questions.q: Why does this lesson split "migrate the catalog app" into two separate pieces?
options: Because Azure requires images and VMs to be migrated by different teams
Because it's really a storage problem (the images) and a compute problem (the app server), and each already has a known pattern
Because storage accounts and virtual machines can't exist in the same resource group
Because the images and the VM must be migrated to different Azure regions
questions.explain: Treating the migration as one blurry task confuses scope. Splitting it into a storage piece and a compute piece turns each into a problem with a known solution pattern.

questions.q: Which of these is explicitly OUT of scope for this Beginner project?
options: Standing up a storage account for the product images
Configuring basic monitoring for the VM
Re-architecting the catalog app into a container platform or serverless design
Standing up a virtual machine for the application server
questions.explain: This project is a lift-and-shift of the existing app as-is, not a redesign. Re-architecting into containers or serverless is explicitly left out.

questions.q: What is the purpose of writing a plain-English target sketch before opening the Azure Portal or CLI?
options: It's a formality Azure requires before creating resources
It bridges the business scope from Lesson 1 to the real resources about to be provisioned, and tests whether the plan is actually clear
It replaces the need for a resource group
It is only useful for presentations, not for planning
questions.explain: If you can't describe the target setup in one clear paragraph, you're not ready to start creating resources yet -- the sketch is the bridge between scope and implementation.

questions.q: Why is scoping out high availability and auto-scaling for this project not "cutting corners"?
options: Because Azure doesn't support high availability for small applications
Because Priya explicitly forbade discussing it
Because it matches the size of the solution to the size of the actual problem -- a reliable, monitored single VM is what this deadline needs
Because high availability is only possible with containers
questions.explain: Scoping down deliberately means matching effort to what was actually asked. The ask was reliability for a launch, not a multi-region zero-downtime architecture.

questions.q: What are the two concrete pieces the catalog app migration actually splits into?
options: A database migration and a networking migration
A static asset migration (product images) and a VM workload migration (the application server)
A monitoring migration and a security migration
A testing migration and a documentation migration
questions.explain: The images need a new home in object storage; the application server needs a new home on a virtual machine. Those are the two real pieces inside the single-sentence ask.
